turns.q:
Your response was: "The summary layout is clear. The "Continue Shopping" button size is distracting. The legal text at bottom is small."

We want to understand what you meant by "The "Continue Shopping" button size is distracting", so let's go a bit deeper. Which of these best captures what you were pointing at?

A) The "Continue Shopping" button appears as a large full-width bar that dominates the lower part of the checkout layout.

B) The "Continue Shopping" button is more visually prominent than the "Place Order" button beneath it, which makes the hierarchy of actions feel out of order.

C) The "Continue Shopping" button takes up a large amount of space between the payment details section and the legal text, making that area feel crowded.

D) None of the above — but only if A, B, and C genuinely miss what you meant; the specific element I was referring to was the "Continue Shopping" button size.

Select A, B, C, or D to continue.
What specifically about the way “Continue Shopping” and “Place Order” are arranged makes “Continue Shopping” read as the higher-priority action here?
turns.a: “Continue Shopping” is black, full-width, and first. “Place Order” is greyed out underneath. That reads as active command versus disabled option. Primary action is visually assigned to leaving checkout.

turns.q: Does that make the checkout’s main action harder to locate in the layout, or does it make the meaning of the “Place Order” button seem unavailable once someone sees it?
turns.a: Both. The main action is buried under the stronger button. “Place Order” looks unavailable because it is grey, low-contrast, and below the exit action.

turns.q: If this layout were built exactly as shown, what would someone likely assume they still need to do before “Place Order” becomes available?
turns.a: Enter payment details. Possibly all fields: card number, expiry, CVV, name. But there is no explicit message tying that to the disabled button.

turns.q: What impact would that stronger “Continue Shopping” placement have on someone trying to understand the next step in this checkout layout?
turns.a: It creates a false next step. After payment fields, the strongest command says leave checkout. A user may think ordering is blocked or secondary until they shop more.

turns.q: If the grey, low-contrast “Place Order” beneath the black “Continue Shopping” were fixed, what would the correct version of that lower checkout area look like?
turns.a: “Place Order” should be the black full-width button directly under Payment Details. “Continue Shopping” should be secondary: smaller, outline, or text link below it. If disabled, “Place Order” needs a visible reason like “Enter payment details to place order.”
